standards_review.notes: all 3 commit subjects in range (EPMCDME-14111: wire ms_teams validation into project settings create/update; EPMCDME-14111: add ms_teams request validation and singleton check; EPMCDME-14111: add ms_teams credential type enum and migration) match the documented 'EPMCDME-####: Description' format

license headers present on all new/changed files (settings_request_validator.py, settings.py, project_settings.py, models.py, alembic migration); code-quality.md explicitly prefers 'X | None' unions over typing.Optional[X] in new code, yet settings_request_validator.py:17 adds a fresh 'from typing import Optional' import specifically to type the new validate_ms_teams_request(..., setting_id: Optional[str] = None) at line 271-272, even though this same module already has 'from __future__ import annotations' (line 15) and already uses the preferred 'IndexInfo | None' style elsewhere (line 424) -- the new signature does not follow the module's own established pattern

validate_ms_teams_request relies on the router's authenticate dependency and existing _check_permission/Ability checks, matching the documented pattern of using the central authentication dependency rather than reimplementing auth; no credentials, tokens, or secrets are introduced or logged by the ms_teams change (only project_name/assistant_ids are logged); assistant_ids list membership is validated via AssistantService.belongs_to_project before use, consistent with existing resource-ownership validators in the same file

blocking_findings.violation: code-quality.md's Types And Imports row says to avoid 'typing.Optional[X]' and prefer 'X | None' unions in new code; the new validate_ms_teams_request function adds 'from typing import Optional' and types setting_id as 'Optional[str] = None' instead of 'str | None = None', despite this module already using 'from __future__ import annotations' and the preferred union style ('IndexInfo | None') elsewhere in the same file
blocking_findings.why_blocking: documented code-quality standard for new code is not met, and the new import/pattern is inconsistent with the module's own already-established style
blocking_findings.remedy: type the parameter as 'setting_id: str | None = None' and drop the new 'Optional' import from the typing import line
